feed.heading: Who he was
life: Prince of Novgorod from 1236, he guided Russia through one of the hardest times in its history, under Tatar rule and threatened from the West. In time of famine he opened his treasury to all who were in need.

Summoned before the Khan, he refused to worship idols, confessing the one God in three Persons. Several times he journeyed to the Golden Horde to plead for his people. Exhausted from his labors, he reposed in 1263, having received the Great Schema.
feed.intercession: Holy Right-believing Prince Alexander, pray to God for us.
feed.caption:
Today (November 23, New Calendar) the Church keeps the feast of the Holy Right-believing Great Prince Alexander Nevsky.

“Nevsky” means “of the Neva.” Prince of Novgorod from 1236, he guided his people through one of the hardest times in Russia’s history, and shone as a truly Christian ruler. In time of famine he opened his treasury to all who were in need. On the night before a battle against far stronger invaders, he was granted a vision of Saints Boris and Gleb in a boat on the Neva, hastening to the aid of “Alexander their kinsman.”

Summoned before the Khan, he said: “I am unable to worship idols because I am a Christian and adore the one and only God in three Persons, the Maker of heaven and earth.” Several times he traveled to the Golden Horde, and even to Mongolia, to plead for relief for his people and to ransom prisoners.

Returning from his last such journey, exhausted and ill from his labors, he gave up his soul to God in 1263. On his deathbed he received the monastic Great Schema and the name Alexis.

Holy Right-believing Prince Alexander, pray to God for us.
